name: Costa Rica (state flag, 1848–1906)
description: Five horizontal stripes of blue, white, red, white and blue in the ratio 1:1:2:1:1, with the 1848 national coat of arms in an oval in the centre of the red stripe.
history: First state version of the flag created in 1848 at the suggestion of Pacífica Fernández, wife of President José María Castro Madriz, who added a red stripe to the Central American blue and white in admiration of the French tricolour; the design was adopted on 29 September 1848 and first hoisted on 12 November 1848. The coat of arms of 1848 sat in the centre of the red stripe. On 27 November 1906 the arms were revised and moved into a white oval set towards the hoist, the arrangement still used on the state flag.
